newsitem.title: USA: APAC falls despite beating EPS consensus.
newsitem.headline: APAC falls despite beating EPS consensus.

text.p: Shares of APAC TeleServices fell nearly 11 percent on Tuesday despite topping fourth quarter earnings estimates, but analysts said Wall Street had hoped the company would beat the consensus by even more.
"The disappointment in my opinion was people were looking for higher than the published numbers," said Wayne Johnson, an analyst for Robertson Stephens.
APAC reported earnings of $0.21 a share versus $0.06 a share last year. According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates was $0.19 a share.
"I think the street was looking for it to be $0.22 or $0.23 even though the consensus was $0.19," Johnson said. "We were at $0.19, and we were happy with the number."
Analysts also pointed out that a lower tax rate for the quarter accounted for a penny of the earnings increase.
APAC was not immediately available for comment.
Shares of APAC, which provides outsourced telephone-based sales, closed down 4-1/8 at 34, the low of the day.
